seats: secular academic scholar of the Bible

fixes.row: (noun form, row order and own_words order)
fixes.why: The noun form opens with the New Testament rows (day of judgment, works, condemnation, mercy, what follows, the world) and only then reaches the Hebrew rows (the poor, justice and righteousness, the gate and court, the king, the LORD's justice). Hebrew mishpat is 240 uses and the weight of the noun form is the court, the poor, the king and the LORD's justice, from which the later eschatological sense is drawn. As built the arc runs backwards: the Hebrew Scriptures are not heard first, and the first row a reader sees is Heb 9:27. The own_words list also begins with Heb 9:27.
fixes.fix: Reorder the noun rows so the Hebrew-led ones come first (justice for the poor; justice and righteousness; the gate and court; the king and the throne; the LORD's justice; justice denied; then judgments on the nations/Israel), then a judge, the world, the day of judgment, works, condemnation, mercy, what follows. Order own_words with Gen 18:25 and Amos 5:24 before Heb 9:27. The order is only the Old-Testament-first order, not a settlement of any doctrine.

fixes.why: The row is headed by a note about judgment by works against being counted righteous by faith, yet several members say something else. Deut 32:4 is 'His work is perfect; all his ways are just': God's work, not people's deeds being judged. Jer 22:13 is a woe on the king who builds 'without justice' and does not pay wages (read in Berean/word-by-word: mishpat here is justice, not a judging of deeds). Jer 7:5 ('correct your ways and deeds, act justly') is a call to act justly. These are in the row because the word for work or deed sits beside the word for justice, and they inflate the row to 15 and put OT verses under a doctrinal note they do not speak to.
fixes.fix: Move Deut 32:4 and Jer 22:13 out (Deut 32:4 already stands in the LORD's justice row; Jer 22:13 belongs in the poor/king rows). Keep Jer 7:5 only if it is relabelled as a call to deeds, otherwise move it to justice for the poor / justice and righteousness. Keep verses where deeds are the ground of the judgment (John 5:29, 2 Cor 5:10, Eccl 12:14, Rom 2:2-5, Jude 15, Jer 1:16, Ezek 7:27).

fixes.row: Judgment and mercy, loving devotion, grace: “mercy triumphs over judgment”
fixes.why: Jude 4 (read in the Berean): ungodly men 'designated long ago for condemnation' who 'turn the grace of our God into a license for immorality'. It is not a pair of judgment and grace; it is grace misused and condemnation of those who misuse it. The row's note says 'the text's own pairs'. Its label also leads with a New Testament quotation (Jas 2:13) while most members are Hebrew mishpat with chesed (Ps 33:5, 89:14, 101:1, Hos 2:19, Mic 6:8, Jer 9:24, Hos 12:6).
fixes.fix: Move Jude 4 to the condemnation or what-follows row. Relabel to lead with the Hebrew pairing: 'Justice with loving devotion, mercy, grace: “the LORD loves righteousness and justice”; “mercy triumphs over judgment”'.

fixes.row: Judgment and what follows, in the text's own words: eternal, fire, destruction, Gehenna
fixes.why: The note says 'the fires of Gehenna (Matt 5:22; 23:33)'. The Berean at Matt 23:33 reads 'How will you escape the sentence of hell?'; there is no fire in that verse. Only 5:22 has 'fire of hell'. The note also puts the phrase 'fires of Gehenna' in quotation marks as if the text said it; the Berean prints 'fire of hell'. Rule 1: a note says only what its verses say.
fixes.fix: Rewrite as “the fire of hell” (Matt 5:22) and “the sentence of hell” (Matt 23:33), noting that the Greek is geenna in both. Drop the quotation marks around 'fires of Gehenna'.

fixes.row: Judgment and the world, the nations
fixes.why: 1 John 4:17 ('confidence on the day of judgment; for in this world we are just like Him') is on the row because the English contains 'world'. It is about the day of judgment and also stands in the day row. The row also joins God judging the nations (Zeph 3:8, Joel, Jer 46:28) with the Servant bringing justice to the nations (Isa 42:1-4, 51:4; Matt 12:18-20), two different movements under one label.
fixes.fix: Remove 1 John 4:17 from this row. Relabel to 'Judgment on the nations; justice for the nations' and add a one-line note that Isa 42 and 51 speak of justice going out to the nations.

fixes.why: The label says 'Justice', which is the Berean's rendering of Hebrew mishpat. Four members use other words: John 16:8 is krisis ('judgment'), Acts 24:25 is 'judgment to come', 2 Cor 3:9 is the 'ministry of condemnation' (katakrisis) beside the ministry of righteousness, and 2 Tim 4:8 is 'righteous Judge' (kritēs). A reader of the label 'Justice' meets 'condemnation' in the third and fourth example slots of different verses. This presents one sense of mishpat as the whole range of these Greek words, and is the pair the hub is most likely to blur. The row is also the largest in the hub (71) and overlaps the LORD's justice (56), the king (24) and the poor rows; Ps 89:14, 97:2, 99:4 and Isa 16:5 each sit in three or four rows.
fixes.fix: Relabel 'Justice and righteousness: the Hebrew pair mishpat and tsedaqah' and move the Greek members (John 16:8, Acts 24:25, 2 Cor 3:9, 2 Tim 4:8) to their own short row 'Judgment, condemnation and righteousness (Greek)', or add a note that the Greek verses use krisis, katakrisis and kritēs, not the word for justice. To cut duplication, keep a verse in the one row where it is most at home and let the door links carry the rest.

fixes.row: Justice denied, perverted, asked for: “God has deprived me of justice”, “Does God pervert justice?”, “Where is the God of justice?”
fixes.why: The label and note frame the row as a complaint against God and the answer ('The complaint and the answer ... the page does not choose'). About half the members are not that. Isa 59:9, read in the Berean: 'Therefore justice is far from us, and righteousness does not reach us', which in Isa 59:2-4 and 59:12-14 is Israel's own sin keeping justice away, not a charge against God. Eccl 3:16 and 5:8 observe human officials perverting justice. Reading Isa 59 into a 'God denies justice' pair is a tilt, and cutting the arc: the human perversion (Isaiah, Ecclesiastes, Habakkuk's 'the wicked hem in the righteous') and the complaint against God (Job, Mal 2:17, Jer 12:1, Isa 40:27) are two different stories.
fixes.fix: Split in two. (a) 'Complaint addressed to God about justice: Job 27:2, 34:12, 40:8; Jer 12:1; Mal 2:17; Isa 40:27; Hab 1:4; Lam 3:35', keeping the present note; (b) 'Justice perverted among people: Eccl 3:16, 5:8; Isa 59:8-15; Hab 1:4; Amos 5:12'. Hab 1:4 may stand in both. If one row is wanted, rewrite the note so it does not call Isa 59 and Eccl a charge against God.

fixes.row: The king and the throne: “the king for judgment”, kings who do justice, the throne
fixes.why: The verb row carries a note that readers take Isa 11:3-4 differently ('whom the verse means ... the page does not choose'). The noun king row holds Isa 9:7, 16:5, 32:1 and Jer 23:5 (the righteous Branch), which readers take of Hezekiah, of David's line, or of the Messiah, and has no note. This is an inconsistency: the same kind of verse is handled by note in one place and not in another. Also Ps 72:1 is of Solomon and has a king-for-the-king prayer that the Old Testament texts themselves frame.
fixes.fix: Add a note on this row: 'In Isa 9:7, 16:5, 32:1 and Jer 23:5 the king is the one the prophet describes, David's heir; readers differ on whom the verses mean, and the page does not choose.' Keep it parallel with the Isa 11 note.

fixes.why: This row is 15% of the noun form and is the catch-all, but a dozen of its New Testament members are judgment falling on a person or an act: 'subject to judgment' (Matt 5:21), 'greater condemnation' (Mark 12:40), 'bring judgment on themselves' (Rom 13:2), 'condemnation is deserved' (Rom 3:8, which is a condemnation, not a leftover). They belong with the argument about what judgment is, and they sit beside Matt 5:22 which is filed under what follows. Filing them as 'other' cuts apart verses that belong together and weakens the New Testament thread. Meanwhile the real oddities (the breastpiece and Urim, the lot, Prov's wise judgment) are mixed in with them.
fixes.fix: Make a row 'Judgment as a warning on particular acts: murder, resisting authority, eating without recognizing the body, teachers, oaths, defrauding widows' with those verses, and leave 'Every other use' for the breastpiece, the Urim and the lot, and the wisdom-literature uses. That also takes the hub from one catch-all of 56 to two smaller rows.

fixes.row: Judged by “the Lord”, “He”, “the One”: the verse does not name him
fixes.why: 'Judged by the Lord' reads as if these are verses where a person is judged by an unnamed judge, yet in Rev 6:10 the verse names its addressee ('O Lord, holy and true'), and in Acts 17:31 it names 'the Man He has appointed'. 'The verse does not name him' is therefore too strong for two of the examples: the text names a title or describes him. The note already says this, but the label does not.
fixes.fix: Relabel 'Judging by one the verse calls “the Lord”, “He”, “the One” or describes: “the Man He has appointed”, “Faithful and True”' and keep the note.

fixes.why: The hub is 26 rows. The worker proposes joins. I would not join 'Told to judge' with 'Told not to judge' (that would put 38 verses in one pile and lose the order the note describes), nor the believing row with the works row (it would merge the very pair the page is declining to settle). But the two rows 'Condemnation, and no condemnation' (noun) and 'Condemn, condemned' (verb) say overlapping things, and so do 'Justice for the poor' and 'Justice and righteousness' on their Hebrew members.
fixes.fix: No merges are needed if the split of 'Justice denied' and the new 'warning' row above are made in exchange for folding 'Justice for the poor' into 'Justice and righteousness' with the poor as a labelled strand; net rows stay at about 26 across two forms. Accept 26 given that noun and verb are separate forms, or fold 'Judged, and believing' (6) into 'Judged, and works' only with a note that each verse stands in the row it fits.

worker_points.point: 1. Final judgment and what follows (eternal punishment, annihilation, universalism); hub silent on Matt 10:28, Rom 11:32, 1 Cor 15:22, Col 1:20 and Matt 25:31-46
worker_points.why: The notes are even-handed and the rows are by the verses' own words. The limit is honest, but the page says 'the hub is silent' only in the worker's report, not on the page. A reader who sees a 'what follows' row with nine verses may take it for the whole text on the subject. Also fix the Matt 23:33 'fires of Gehenna' wording (see fixes).

worker_points.point: 2. Judgment by works beside being counted righteous by faith (works rows 15; believing rows 6)
worker_points.why: The pairing and the 'takes no side' note are right in both forms. The small believing row (6) is accurate about the data, and Rom 14:22-23 ('whoever doubts is condemned') and Heb 11:7 are about conscience and Noah, so the row is thinner than it looks; but the works row is padded with non-judging verses (Deut 32:4, Jer 22:13). Cut those so the two sit fairly.

worker_points.point: 3. God's justice in Israel's courts kept as its own sense; Isa 53:8 and Acts 8:33 in the courts row
worker_points.why: Keeping the court, the poor and the king as their own Hebrew sense is the right instinct and is what the Hebrew Scriptures need. Isa 53:8 and Acts 8:33 stand as words ('judgment', 'justice') in a trial-and-sentence row with no reading of who is meant; that is neutral. The only objection is the row order (see the first fix).

worker_points.point: 4. Divine persons by hand ('God judges' 89, 'Jesus' 11, 'the Lord, He, the One' 9, 'A judge, the Judge')
worker_points.why: Assignment is by hand, and the note says readers take the unnamed ones of the Father or of Christ without choosing. The 'God judges' row contains 1 Pet 2:23 and John 5:22-30 areas correctly separated. Only the label wording of the 'unnamed' row needs the small fix above.

worker_points.point: 5. 'Do not judge' and 'judge righteously' in adjacent rows; rebukes of judging included (Rom 2:1, 2:3, Jas 4:11-12)
worker_points.why: The 'Told not to judge, and rebuked for judging' label now says what its verses say. Matt 7:1, Rom 14:4, Jas 4:12 and Col 2:16 are fitting. John 7:24 and 1 Cor 5:12 stand in both rows, which is correct. The note on the 'told not to' row is null; the 'told to judge' row carries the 'page does not say how reconciled' note for both. Acceptable.

worker_points.point: 6. Isa 11:3-4 in the judges row with a note that readers differ on whom it means
worker_points.why: The note is right but is applied to one verse only. Isa 9:7, 16:5, 32:1, Jer 23:5 in the noun king row are the same kind of verse and have no note (see the king-row fix).

worker_points.point: 7. Mark 16:16 (longer ending) in the believing row and condemn row, flagged in both notes
worker_points.why: Flagged where it stands, in line with the site-wide marking of Mark 16:9-20.

worker_points.point: 8. Hard verses kept: Rev 20:12-13, 1 Pet 4:6; the Job/prophets complaint row beside Job 34:12
worker_points.why: Rev 20:12-13 and 1 Pet 4:6 are right to keep. The complaint row, though, mixes complaints against God with human perversion of justice (Isa 59, Eccl 3:16, 5:8); split it (see the fix).

worker_points.point: 9. Placement: Rom 2:5 and 2 Thess 1:5 in the LORD's justice row; Ezek 21:27 under 'Every other use'
worker_points.why: 'Righteous judgment of God' being about the quality of the judgment is a defensible placement, and Rom 2:5 also stands in the works row. Leaving Ezek 21:27 unplaced because readers differ is neutral. Rom 2:5 could also be added to the day row, since the verse says 'the day of wrath'.

missing.what: The Hebrew 'day of the LORD' texts, which are the Old Testament side of the 'day of judgment' row but contain no judgment word: without them the day row is almost wholly New Testament (only Ps 1:5 and Dan 7). The arc from the day of the LORD to the day of judgment is cut. A note or door on the day row would show it.

Matt 25:31-46 (the sheep and goats) has no judgment word, so it is not in any row, and 'the hub is silent on it' is not stated on the page; it is the central judgment scene of the Gospels and sits in the card's gather list only. A note on the day row, or a door to the gather card, would tell the reader it is gathered elsewhere.

The Greek court verb for the verdict itself, 'justify' (dikaioo), which is the other side of condemnation in Rom 5:16-18 and 8:33-34; the worker leaves it to the righteousness hub, and a door from the condemnation row to righteousness would keep the pair together.

examples_checked: 26 of 26 rows' examples show their label in the Berean, with these qualifications: the 'Judgment and works' row's Deut 32:4 and Jer 22:13 do not speak of a judging of deeds; 'Justice and righteousness' has Greek examples (John 16:8) that the label 'Justice' does not name; the 'Justice denied' row's Isa 59 members are human perversion, not a charge against God; 'Judgment and mercy' has Jude 4 in its member list. All the first examples, and the other three examples in each of the remaining rows, fit.
summary: The hub is faithful to the words and keeps the doctrinal pairs side by side without a verdict, and the Hebrew sense of mishpat is kept apart from the Greek eschatology. It needs the Hebrew rows put first, a handful of misfit verses moved (Deut 32:4, Jer 22:13, Jude 4, 1 John 4:17), the justice-denied row split, the Greek members of 'Justice and righteousness' named, the Matt 23:33 note corrected, and the NT warnings gathered out of the catch-all row.
